 Trey Kaufman-Renn is joining Kansas, giving Bill Self's Jayhawks a proven frontcourt scorer with extensive Big Ten and NCAA Tournament experience. Kansas announced the addition Monday with a "Welcome to the fam, TKR" post, and ESPN's Jeff Borzello reported that Kaufman-Renn had signed with the program. He arrives after five seasons at Purdue and a court ruling that allows him to pursue another year of college eligibility while his case against the NCAA continues.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Kaufman-Renn gives Kansas a productive veteran forward
 Kaufman-Renn averaged 14.2 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game in 2025-26, his final season at Purdue. He shot 57.8% from the field and appeared in 37 games. Across his Boilermakers career, the 6-foot-9 forward played 147 games and made 112 starts.
 That resume gives Kansas a player who can contribute as a scorer and rebounder from the start. Kaufman-Renn can finish near the basket, create opportunities for teammates and provide a physical presence on the glass. His experience also gives Self another option with a long track record in high-pressure college games.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The addition is particularly notable because Kaufman-Renn played for a Purdue program that reached three consecutive Elite Eights. He was a first-team All-Big Ten selection in 2025 and an honorable mention All-American, establishing himself as one of the conference's most productive forwards.
 MORE : Kansas freshman Tyran Stokes receives major honor as Big 12 poll delivers surprising Jayhawks verdict 
 A remarkable path from Purdue to Lawrence
 Kaufman-Renn's return to college basketball follows an unusual route. He redshirted his first season at Purdue after a knee injury, then played four seasons for the Boilermakers. Minnesota selected him with the 59th pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, but he pursued another year of college eligibility through the courts.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A Clark County judge granted Kaufman-Renn a preliminary injunction against the NCAA on Oct. 9, extending his eligibility while the case continues. That ruling opened the door for him to join a team, and Kansas has now secured his services.
 For Kansas, the move adds a veteran who can strengthen the frontcourt and take on a meaningful role. Kaufman-Renn's scoring and rebounding should give the Jayhawks another proven option as Self shapes the rotation for the season ahead.
